translations.text: From the holy day of Easter fifty days are counted to this day, and this day is called Pentecost, that is, the fiftieth day of the Easter season.
This day was established and made holy in the old law. God commanded Moses in the land of Egypt that he and all the people of Israel should offer to God, in every household, a lamb one year old,

and mark the sign of the cross with its blood on their doorposts and lintels. Then on that night God's angel went out and killed, in every house of the Egyptian people, the firstborn and dearest child.
And the people of Israel went out of that country on the same night, and God led them across the Red Sea on dry feet. Then Pharaoh pressed after them with a great army.
When he came into the middle of the sea, God's people had already gone up out of it, and God then drowned Pharaoh and all his host.
Then God commanded Moses and the people to keep that season with great reverence at the turn of every year.
That season was then appointed for the people as the Easter season, because God had rescued them from their enemies and destroyed their persecutors.
Then about fifty days after that, God gave the people the law, and God's glory was seen up on a mountain called Sinai.
A great light came there, and a terrifying sound, and trumpets blowing. Then God called Moses to him, and he was with God for forty days, and wrote down the old law at God's direction.
Then [the fiftieth day after it] was called the day of Pentecost in the Old Law.
The lamb that was offered signified the slaying of Christ, who, though innocent, was offered to his Father for our redemption.

Now his passion and his resurrection are our Easter season, because he redeemed us from the devil's slavery, and our persecutors are drowned through holy baptism, just as Pharaoh and his people were in the Red Sea.
These fifty days from the day of Easter are all made holy as one celebration, and this present day is our Pentecost, that is, the fiftieth day from Easter Day.
On the old Pentecost God gave the law to the people of Israel, and on this day the Holy Spirit came in the form of fire to God's household;
Therefore, just as the lamb signified Christ's passion, so also the old law signified the preaching of the gospel under God's grace.
There are three ages in this world: one is the age that was without law; the second is the one that was under the law; the third is now, after Christ's coming. This age is called 'under God's grace.'
We are not without law, nor may we keep the law of Moses bodily, but God's grace guides us to his will, if we are mindful of Christ's commandments and the apostles' teaching.
It is told in this epistle reading how the Holy Spirit came on this day to the faithful company of Christ's household.
Luke the Evangelist wrote in the book 'Acts of the Apostles' that "the holy household was continuing with one mind in prayer in an upper room after Christ's ascension, waiting for his promise;
Then on this day, which is called Pentecost, a great sound suddenly came from heaven and filled the whole upper room with fire;
and there appeared above each of them something like tongues of fire, and they were then all filled with the Holy Spirit, and began to speak in various languages, as the Holy Spirit taught them.

Then there were gathered in the city of Jerusalem devout men from every nation that dwells under heaven; and the apostles spoke to the gathering of the people, and each of them recognized his own language."
"Then the multitude was greatly amazed, and they said in wonder, 'Lo, are not these who are speaking here Galileans?
And each of us has heard them speak in our own languages, in which we were born! We have heard them speak of the great works of God in our own languages!
Lo, what can this be?' Then the Jews said mockingly, 'These men are drunk with new wine.'
Then Peter answered, 'It is the third hour of the morning; how could we be drunk at this hour? But the saying of the prophet Joel is now fulfilled.

God said through the prophet's mouth that he would send his Spirit upon human flesh; "and the children of men shall prophesy, and I will give my wonders from above, from the heavens, and my signs down on the earth."
Know truly that Christ arose from death, and ascended to heaven as we witnessed, and sits at his Father's right hand, just as David prophesied about him,
saying: "The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand, until I lay your enemies under your footstool."
When the people heard this, they were cut to the heart, and said to the apostles, "Sirs, what must we do?"
Then Peter answered, "Repent of your sins, and receive baptism in Christ's name, and your sins will be blotted out, and you will receive the Holy Spirit."
Then they received his teaching, and on that day three thousand people turned to baptism.
Then they were all in unity with the apostles, and sold their possessions, and handed the money over to the apostles, and they distributed it to each according to his need."
"Again, at another preaching, five thousand men believed in Christ, and the whole multitude of believers became so united in mind as if they all had one heart and one soul;
none of them had private possessions, but all their things were common to them all, nor was there any poor person among them.
Those who had landed property sold it, and brought the price to the feet of the apostles: they then distributed it to each according to his need."

"Then God worked many signs among the people through the hands of the apostles, so that they laid the sick along the street where Peter went by, and as soon as his shadow touched them, they were healed of all infirmities.
Then a great multitude came running from the nearby towns, and brought their sick and those possessed by devils, and they were all healed at the apostles' hands.
They laid their hands on believing people, and they received the Holy Spirit."
"There was a certain thane named Ananias, and his wife Sapphira. They said to each other that they wanted to join the apostles' fellowship.
They then decided that it would be safer for them to keep back some part of the price of their land, in case something should happen to them.
Then the thane came to the apostles with the money. Peter said, "Ananias, the devil has deceived your heart, and you have lied to the Holy Spirit.
Why did you want to act deceitfully with what was your own? You have not lied to men, but to God." When he heard these words, he fell down and died.
When he had been buried, his wife Sapphira came, not knowing what had happened to her husband. Then Peter said, "Tell me, did you sell the land for this much?"
She answered, "Yes, sir, that much." Then Peter said again, "Why did you two agree on this, that you dared to test God?"
She fell down at once and died, and she was buried beside her husband. Then great fear came upon God's church and upon all who learned of it."
Afterwards, before they dispersed, the apostles set James, who was called the Just, on Christ's seat, and the whole faithful church obeyed him, according to God's teaching.
He then occupied that seat for thirty years, and after him Simeon, the Saviour's kinsman.

Following that example, the monastic life was established with this rule: that they live in a monastery under their superior's direction, in chastity, and that their possessions be common to all, as the apostles instituted it.
You heard a little earlier, in this reading, that the Holy Spirit came upon the apostles in fiery tongues, and gave them knowledge of all languages;
because the humble company earned from God what the proud host had lost long before.
It happened after Noah's flood that giants wanted to build a city, and a tower so high that its top would rise up to heaven.
At that time there was one language among all mankind, and the work was begun against God's will.
For that reason God also scattered them, so that he gave each of the workers a strange language, and none of them could understand another's speech.
They then stopped the building and scattered across the whole world; and from then on there were as many languages as there were workmen.
Now again on this day, through the coming of the Holy Spirit, all languages were united and brought into harmony, because the whole holy company of Christ's household was speaking in all languages;
and what was also more wonderful, when one of them preached in one language, it seemed to each who heard the preaching as if he were speaking in his own language,
whether they were Hebrews, or Greeks, or Romans, or Egyptians, or of whatever nation they were who heard the teaching.
In this fellowship their humility earned this power, and the giants' pride earned confusion.
The Holy Spirit appeared over the apostles in the form of fire, and over Christ, at his baptism, in the likeness of a dove. Why over Christ in the form of a dove?
Why over Christ's household in the likeness of fire? It is read in books about that kind of bird that its nature is very gentle, and innocent, and peaceable.
The Saviour is the judge of all mankind, but he did not come to judge mankind, as he himself said, but to save it.
If he had wished to judge mankind when he first came to the world, who would then have been saved?

For he did not wish to condemn the sinful by his coming, but wished to gather them into his kingdom. First he wished to guide us with gentleness, so that afterwards he might preserve us at his judgement.
Therefore the Holy Spirit was seen above Christ in the likeness of a dove, because he lived in this world with gentleness, and innocence, and peaceableness.
He did not cry out, nor was he bitter of speech, nor did he stir up strife, but he bore with men's wickedness through his gentleness.
But he who was gentle at the first coming, for the conversion of sinners, will pass stern judgment on the careless at the second coming.
The Holy Spirit was seen in fiery tongues above the apostles, because he made them burn with zeal for God's will and preach about God's kingdom.

They had fiery tongues when they preached God's glories with love, so that the hearts of the heathen, which were cold through unbelief and fleshly desires, might be kindled toward the heavenly commandments.
If the Holy Spirit does not teach a man's mind within, the preacher's words proclaimed outwardly are in vain. It is the nature of fire that it consumes whatever is near it:
So shall the teacher do who is inspired by the Holy Spirit: first quench every vice in himself, and afterwards in those under him.
God's Spirit appeared in the likeness of a dove and in the form of fire, because he makes those whom he fills with his grace gentle in innocence and burning with zeal for God's will.
Simplicity is not pleasing to God without wisdom, nor wisdom without simplicity; as it is said of the blessed Job, that he was simple and righteous.
What is righteousness without gentleness? Or what is gentleness without righteousness?
But the Holy Spirit, who teaches righteousness and gentleness, had to appear both in fire and in a dove,
because he makes the hearts of the people whom he enlightens with his grace gentle through innocence and kindled through love and wisdom.
God is, as Paul said, a consuming fire. He is an unspeakable fire, and invisible. Of that fire the Saviour said,
"I came because I wished to send fire on earth, and I will that it burn." He sent the Holy Spirit to earth, and with his breath he kindled the hearts of earthly men.
The earth burns when the heart of earthly man, which was before cold through fleshly desires, is set alight with the love of God.
The Holy Spirit does not dwell in his own nature as he was seen, for he is invisible; but for the sake of the symbolism, as we said before, he appeared in a dove and in fire.
He is called in the Greek language Paraclete, that is, Comforter-Spirit, because he comforts the sorrowful who repent of their sins, and gives them hope of forgiveness, and soothes their sad minds.
He forgives sins, and he is the way to the forgiveness of all sins. He gives his grace to whom he wills.

To one man he gives wisdom and speech, to another good understanding, to another great faith, to another power to heal the sick, to another prophecy, to another the discernment of good and evil spirits;
to another he gives various tongues, to another the interpretation of various languages. The Holy Spirit does all these things, distributing to each as it pleases him;
for he is the Almighty Maker, and as soon as he enlightens a man's mind, he turns it from evil to good.
He enlightened David's heart when in his youth he loved the harp, and made him a psalmist. There was a herdsman named Amos, whom the Holy Spirit turned into a great prophet.
Peter was a fisherman, whom the same Spirit of God turned into an apostle. Paul persecuted Christians, and he chose him as teacher to all nations.
Matthew was a tax collector, whom he turned into an evangelist. The apostles did not dare to preach the true faith for fear of the Jewish people;
But after they were set on fire by the Holy Spirit, they despised all bodily torments, and fearlessly preached the glories of God.
The honour of this day is to be celebrated, because Almighty God, that is, the Holy Spirit, humbled himself so that he would visit the children of men at this time.
At Christ's birth the Almighty Son of God was made a human man, and on this day believing men became gods, just as Christ said,
"I said, You are gods, and you are all children of the Most High." The chosen are God's children, and also gods, not by nature, but through the grace of the Holy Spirit.
One God is by nature in three persons: the Father, and his Son, that is, his Wisdom, and the Holy Spirit, who is the Love and Will of them both.
Their nature is indivisible, ever abiding in one Godhead. Yet the same one said of his chosen, "You are gods."
Through Christ's incarnation men were redeemed from the devil's bondage, and through the coming of the Holy Spirit, human men were made gods.
Christ took on human nature at his coming, and men received God through the visitation of the Holy Spirit. The man who does not have God's Spirit in him is not God's.
Every person's works show which spirit guides him. God's Spirit always guides toward holiness and goodness; the devil's spirit guides toward vices and wicked deeds.
The Holy Spirit came twice upon the apostles. Christ breathed the Holy Spirit upon the apostles before his ascension, saying, "Receive the Holy Spirit."
Again, on this day, the Almighty Father and the Son sent the Spirit of them both to the faithful company dwelling in this world.
The Saviour breathed his Spirit upon his disciples, as a sign that they and all Christian men should love their neighbours as themselves.
Afterwards, as he had promised before, he sent the same Spirit from heaven, so that we should love God above all other things.
The Holy Spirit is one, though he came twice upon the apostles. In the same way there is one love and two commandments: that we must love God and our fellow people.
But we must learn through men how we may come to the love of God, just as John the apostle said,
"He who does not love his brother, whom he sees, how can he love God, whom he does not see bodily?"
We honour the coming of the Holy Spirit with hymns for seven days, because he inspires our minds with a sevenfold gift,
that is, with wisdom and understanding, with counsel and strength, with knowledge and piety, and he fills us with the fear of God.
Whoever comes through good merits to these sevenfold gifts of the Holy Spirit then has every honour.
But he who wishes to come to this honour must believe in the Holy Trinity and in the True Unity,
that the Father, and his Son, and the Spirit of them both are three in persons, and one indivisible God, abiding in one Godhead.
This faith was signified by the three thousand who first turned to the faith after the coming of the Holy Spirit.
Just as the three thousand were one company, so the Holy Trinity is one God. And that company was so united in mind that it was as though they all had one heart and one soul;
because the Holy Trinity has one Godhead, and one nature, and one will, and one work, inseparably.
The faithful brought their money and laid it at the apostles' feet. By this it is shown that Christian men should not set their hope on worldly treasure, but on God alone.
The covetous man who sets his hope on his hoard of gold is, as the apostle said, "like one who practises idolatry."
They held the gold as worthless, because covetousness had no place in their hearts; therefore they held their possessions in common, so that they might live in true peace without covetousness.
They laid their hands on faithful men, and the Holy Spirit came to them through their confirmation.
Bishops are of the same order in God's church, and they keep that ordinance in their episcopal office, in that they lay their hands on baptized people
and pray that the Almighty Ruler, who lives and reigns forever without end, send them the sevenfold gift of his Spirit. Amen.
